^You come upon an old warty woman with the face of a hag. Her ugly old mouth is filled with rotten teeth and the clothes she wears are tattered rags. At her feet is a jet-black cat that hisses at you when you approach.

"Will you help a poor old woman?" the hag inquires in a frail voice. "A small purse of gold--1000 coins should be enough--is all I ask..."^

args.raw: ^How dare the evil witch ask you for money! Do you slay her where she stands?^
args.text: How dare the evil witch ask you for money! Do you slay her where she stands?

args.raw: ^You step up to the witch, and with a mighty lunge, impale her with your sword! As her life slowly drains from her withered body, she screams a hideous scream. ^The hag eyes the troglodytes and grins a wicked toothy grin.

Cackling evilly, the old woman vanishes into her hut and slams the door.^

^You pause a moment to ponder what just occurred...

Aside from her curse, that witch died rather easily. You have an eerie feeling that you haven't seen the last of her.^

args.raw: ^Your thoughts are troubled as you leave behind the battle carnage that took place outside this elven community. Are you really in league with an evil witch? args.raw:
^You reach a larger community of elves, but they are suspicious. You explain what happened, and they sympathize but are sad that the evil witch still lives.

"She'll have gone into hiding now and you'll never catch up with her. She'll bide her time and then terrorize us some more. I'm afraid we can't help you much, but Sandoran wants adventure so he'll come with you if you like. And here's a ring you might find useful. You gratefully accept the ring and welcome the company of this charming young elf boy."^

You gratefully accept the ring and welcome the company of this charming young elf boy."

args.raw: ^Nagging worries about the evil witch you failed to kill plague you as you leave behind the elven community and continue on your quest. But you know there's no sense in going back--as the elves said, you would not find her now, and you can't hang around here forever.^

args.raw:
^You approach the earth elementals and demand that they return the stolen Tome of Earth Magic. The elementals glower and shout back:

"IT BELONGED TO US FIRST. THAT CONNIVING MAGICIAN STOLE IT FROM US. WE WERE ONLY TAKING BACK WHAT WAS RIGHTFULLY OURS!"

Can you believe them? Does it matter if you do? You need the book to complete your quest so that you can rid the world of the necromancer, Zarachodar. So be it, you prepare to fight them! The elementals prepare for battle too--their strongest leader mounts a horse and faces you, challenging you to make the first move!^

^You hear a shout from the northern passage. It's your old friend, Vandula! It's been years since you've seen him--what could he be doing down here?

"Hail Vandula!" you call out.

"Lydorie!" he shouts back. "It's great to see you! I stepped through a one-way portal and found myself down here in the midst of these snake-haired women. Just one moment while I kill some more."^

^The robed man speaks to you in a soft voice.

"I am the guardian of the burning bridge. Answer me these questions three if the other side you wish to see."

His eyes bore into your brain and you feel that he knows all about you.^
args.text:
The robed man speaks to you in a soft voice.

"I am the guardian of the burning bridge. Answer me these questions three if the other side you wish to see."

His eyes bore into your brain and you feel that he knows all about you.

args.raw:
^{"The first question."}

"Are you Lydorie, battle mage of Battlement?"^
args.text:
{"The first question."}

"Are you Lydorie, battle mage of Battlement?"

args.raw:
^"DO NOT MOCK ME WITH YOUR PETTY DECEPTION!"

"Those who lie about their identity are only fit to lead the peasants. That shall be your new title, and your new ability too. 'Master of Peasants'."^
args.text:
"DO NOT MOCK ME WITH YOUR PETTY DECEPTION!"

"Those who lie about their identity are only fit to lead the peasants. That shall be your new title, and your new ability too. 'Master of Peasants'."

args.raw: ^"Good, you are wise to not try and deceive me. We shall continue."^
args.text: "Good, you are wise to not try and deceive me. We shall continue."

args.raw:
^{"The second question."}

"Do you believe that the witch was guilty of the alleged evil doing she was accused of?"^
args.text:
{"The second question."}

"Do you believe that the witch was guilty of the alleged evil doing she was accused of?"

args.raw: ^"Yes, I see it in your actions. You are a true friend to elves, and so I bring to you many strong and loyal grand elf warriors."^
args.text: "Yes, I see it in your actions. You are a true friend to elves, and so I bring to you many strong and loyal grand elf warriors."

args.raw: ^"I also bestow upon you the gift to transform goblins, hobgoblins, orcs and orc chieftains into grand elves."^
args.text: "I also bestow upon you the gift to transform goblins, hobgoblins, orcs and orc chieftains into grand elves."

args.raw: ^"You killed the witch yet you don't believe she was guilty? You are a hypocrite. You do not deserve those elves or that magic bow, so I take them from you!"^
args.text: "You killed the witch yet you don't believe she was guilty? You are a hypocrite. You do not deserve those elves or that magic bow, so I take them from you!"

args.raw: ^"If you believed she was guilty, then why did you aid her? Or perhaps you have now changed your mind? To bless or to curse? You do not know, so I take from you those spells."^
args.text: "If you believed she was guilty, then why did you aid her? Or perhaps you have now changed your mind? To bless or to curse? You do not know, so I take from you those spells."

args.raw: ^"You aided the witch and you stand by your beliefs. Very commendable! I grant you an increase in your combat abilities and magical power."^
args.text: "You aided the witch and you stand by your beliefs. Very commendable! I grant you an increase in your combat abilities and magical power."

args.raw: ^"You believe the witch is guilty? Then why did you not slay her when you had the chance? You are WEAK! I take from you your ability in combat, since you do not deserve it."^
args.text: "You believe the witch is guilty? Then why did you not slay her when you had the chance? You are WEAK! I take from you your ability in combat, since you do not deserve it."

args.raw: ^"You do not believe the witch was guilty? So why did you spit upon her? You lack wisdom, therefore, I strip it from you!"^
args.text: "You do not believe the witch was guilty? So why did you spit upon her? You lack wisdom, therefore, I strip it from you!"

args.raw:
^{"The final question."}

"Have you embraced the dark arts of Necromancy?"^
args.text:
{"The final question."}

"Have you embraced the dark arts of Necromancy?"

args.raw: ^"So, you intend to fight darkness with darkness? Evil with evil? You are a misguided fool! But so be it, I can help you no more until you are ready to help yourself."^
args.text: "So, you intend to fight darkness with darkness? Evil with evil? You are a misguided fool! But so be it, I can help you no more until you are ready to help yourself."

args.raw: ^"You think you can hide your dark arts from me? Or perhaps you are ashamed of them. Very well, I strip you of your powers of Necromancy. And now I must go."^
args.text: "You think you can hide your dark arts from me? Or perhaps you are ashamed of them. Very well, I strip you of your powers of Necromancy. And now I must go."

args.raw: ^"You turned down the spirits' gift of Necromancy yet you claim to have embraced it? You are a very confused woman. I give you the Badge of Courage, and hope that it will give you the courage to be true to your convictions. Go now."^
args.text: "You turned down the spirits' gift of Necromancy yet you claim to have embraced it? You are a very confused woman. I give you the Badge of Courage, and hope that it will give you the courage to be true to your convictions. Go now."

args.raw: ^"You made a wise choice when you turned down the spirits' gift of Necromancy. You cannot fight darkness with darkness. Take this sword, The Sword of Judgement, and use it for justice."^
args.text: "You made a wise choice when you turned down the spirits' gift of Necromancy. You cannot fight darkness with darkness. Take this sword, The Sword of Judgement, and use it for justice."

args.raw:
^Gerfrex and her six clones eagerly join you, anxious to toast a vile necromancer named Zarachodar.

"I think Zarachodar is a bit afraid of me," sniggers Gerfrex. "That's probably why he left me with my hoard while waiting for the Dark Sun and working on his transformation spell. That stupid old bag of bones!"

Gerfrex offers to teach you a temporary version of the Clone spell she's used on herself. "Very useful. Much fun!" she chortles.^

args.raw: ^You've spotted what looks like a hidden cave! But you can't figure out how to reach it. The rocks and debris here are unstable and your attempts to reach the opening result in several terrifying rockfalls.^
args.text: You've spotted what looks like a hidden cave! But you can't figure out how to reach it. The rocks and debris here are unstable and your attempts to reach the opening result in several terrifying rockfalls.

args.raw: ^If only you were more skilled at finding your way and navigating impossible paths you might be able to get through the cave tunnel.^
args.text: If only you were more skilled at finding your way and navigating impossible paths you might be able to get through the cave tunnel.

args.raw: ^Thankful for Crag Hack's skill at finding paths, you follow his lead and enter the hidden mountain tunnel.^
args.text: Thankful for Crag Hack's skill at finding paths, you follow his lead and enter the hidden mountain tunnel.

args.raw: ^A hidden cave! You've discovered a way through the mountain after all. It's a good thing you're so skilled in pathfinding (unlike your sister Lydorie).^
args.text: A hidden cave! You've discovered a way through the mountain after all. It's a good thing you're so skilled in pathfinding (unlike your sister Lydorie).

args.raw: ^With a bit of effort, you're able to clear away the rubble from the previous cave-in and travel through the mountain tunnel.^
args.text: With a bit of effort, you're able to clear away the rubble from the previous cave-in and travel through the mountain tunnel.

args.raw: ^This tunnel smells of death, doom and decay, and suddenly Lydorie sees a deeply unsettling vision of the future. In it, {SHE} is the Dark Necromancer whom all the world despises. It is {SHE} who commands death to all life. Lydorie feels utterly repulsed by the vile creature she has become--how could this have happened? Then the face of the Mad Monk, Guardian of the Burning Bridge, flashes into her mind and she silently calls for help...^
args.text: This tunnel smells of death, doom and decay, and suddenly Lydorie sees a deeply unsettling vision of the future. In it, {SHE} is the Dark Necromancer whom all the world despises. It is {SHE} who commands death to all life. Lydorie feels utterly repulsed by the vile creature she has become--how could this have happened? Then the face of the Mad Monk, Guardian of the Burning Bridge, flashes into her mind and she silently calls for help...

args.raw: ^Within moments, Lydorie feels waves of light descending upon her, and the evil that has tainted her soul is washed away. Her army is transformed to living creatures once again and her spirit rejoices!^
args.text: Within moments, Lydorie feels waves of light descending upon her, and the evil that has tainted her soul is washed away. Her army is transformed to living creatures once again and her spirit rejoices!

args.raw: ^You make it through the tunnel and call out to Lydorie to join you. "Just follow my footsteps and you'll be fine."^
args.text: You make it through the tunnel and call out to Lydorie to join you. "Just follow my footsteps and you'll be fine."

args.raw: ^You exit the cave on the other side of the mountain just in time to avoid being crushed by huge boulders that crash down behind you, blocking your return. The passage you traversed must have been unstable. There's no going back now!^

args.raw: ^The Cloak of the Undead King suddenly animates, rising into the air. Like a bat with dark flapping wings, it flies towards the Necropolis and vanishes between the bars of a dark tower window.^
args.text: The Cloak of the Undead King suddenly animates, rising into the air. Like a bat with dark flapping wings, it flies towards the Necropolis and vanishes between the bars of a dark tower window.

args.raw:
^The voice of Zarachodar booms out from the castle.

"SO, YOU HAVE RETURNED MY CLOAK! HOW CONSIDERATE OF YOU. NOW GO, LITTLE MORSEL, WHILE YOUR PITIFUL LIFE STILL EXISTS."^
